title: Chapter 261: The Map Is Wrong?
html:
“All right. Don’t worry.” Gu Feiyu could not understand why Chen Ge needed to barricade the exit merely to frighten visitors. Is he trying to fill them with despair?

Once Chen Ge had gone below, the dutiful Xiao Gu closed the wooden boards and hauled the props into place.

…

The visitors followed the left-hand path until they reached another intersection. “This is the second junction. The left passage leads to the Deep Well, while the corridor on the right ends at three empty rooms.”

Yang Chen consulted his notebook, which described every scene in detail. His seniors’ ability to remember everything so vividly even after returning to school testified to the depth of the despair they had endured.

“Each room has its own number. A woman’s body is hidden in the ceiling above one bathroom, and according to the notes, there’s a name tag in her pocket.”

Li Xue and Wang Dan frowned at the description. Merely hearing it drained their desire to continue.

“Leave this name tag to us,” Kong Xiangming said suddenly. Wei Wu opened his mouth to object, but a glance from his companion silenced him.

“All right. Should we wait outside? According to the notebook, mannequins may interfere once visitors enter the room.”

“No need. Didn’t you say time was running out? Take the other path, and we’ll rejoin you later.” Kong Xiangming departed immediately. Wei Wu followed, and neither spoke as they walked away.

“Yang Chen, let’s go.” Wang Dan pointed down the other corridor and whispered, “Splitting up is better. Now we don’t have to watch them.”

The notebook warned against separating, but this was an unusual situation; the other two visitors were probably actors. Yang Chen nodded, and the three students jogged to the Deep Well. Just as the notes promised, two name tags lay inside.

“Two name tags. The seniors were right—this well is extremely dangerous.” Li Xue drew a ball of string from her purse, removed her hair clip, and tied it to one end. “Fortunately, we came prepared.”

“The boss won’t have anticipated this.” For the first time inside the Haunted House, the students felt a spark of triumph. Li Xue lowered her makeshift fishing line and easily hooked one of the name tags. As she slowly reeled it from the well, all three exhaled as though they had won a championship.

“Well done!” When Li Xue lowered the line again, the well seemed to have deepened. Several attempts later, she finally hooked the second name tag—but as she began to pull, something horrifying happened.

The sand shifted, revealing a corpse’s face. Half the name tag protruded from the sand; the other half rested between the dead person’s lips.

“F*ck me!”

“What the hell?!”

All three gasped. For the first time, they understood just how malicious the adult world could be.

“Xiao Xue, pull harder. See if you can wrench the name tag free.”

The girl tugged the string. Sand rolled aside, and the body began to rise.

After several attempts, the string snapped. The name tag remained at the bottom, and her hair clip now lay beside the mannequin’s lips.

“This won’t work. The boss didn’t leave us any chance at all!” Li Xue gazed regretfully at her lost hair clip.

“Stay here. I’ll retrieve the clip and name tag.” Wang Dan braced his hands against the well. “It’s only a mannequin made to resemble a corpse. We’ve seen real bodies.”

“Have you ever seen one that moves?” Yang Chen stopped him. “The seniors marked this well as extremely dangerous. It’s only one name tag; we can clear the scenario by finding others. Don’t risk everything for such a small reward.”

“You’re right.” Wang Dan was rash, not foolish. “Should we ask those two actors to climb down for us?”

“If they’re actors, they’ll refuse. If they’re ordinary visitors, asking would be immoral,” Li Xue pointed out.

“We still have time. We didn’t pass the couple, so they probably took the other route. Let’s meet up with them first.” Yang Chen checked the map. “A connecting passage beside the Deep Well should lead to the girls’ dormitory.”

Yang Chen followed the map, but instead of the girls’ dormitory, they found another junction.

“The map is wrong?”

Yang Chen rotated the map in confusion. “How can there be another route? Did we trigger a hidden scenario? Is this one of Boss Chen’s new tricks?”

The students exchanged uneasy looks. The map on which they had depended was now useless.

“No wonder the earlier areas contained so few name tags. Some must have been moved into this hidden scenario.” Yang Chen tore a page from the notebook and began sketching the new route. “Come on. Even if we don’t clear it today, we can at least update the map for everyone else.”

Thus, the three students became the first visitors to enter Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy. Beyond the corner, the building’s architecture changed. The scorch marks vanished, and the surroundings looked far more realistic.

“Yang Chen, do you smell that?” Wang Dan stopped at the entrance and covered his nose. “Something in there has gone rotten.”

…

Kong Xiangming stood silently outside the Room of Three.

“Why did we avoid the students to come here?” Wei Wu asked.

“Look around. Doesn’t this resemble Hai Ming Apartments?” Kong Xiangming opened the door. The similarity was unmistakable.

“You’re right. This cannot be a coincidence.” Wei Wu stared in surprise. “We went to Hai Ming Apartments only a few days ago to capture that fugitive, and now we find the building reproduced here.”

“Constructing something on this scale would take time. The boss must have uncovered Hai Ming Apartments’ secret long ago,” Kong Xiangming reasoned. “He may even have seen the person who escaped from behind the door.”
